adjudication_rationale: It reports only general improvement on most metrics and two examples, omitting the five-metric pattern and the XNLI and Lambada decreases.
It claims higher MMLU than simple methods in both settings, but in 1B Method M tied ZeroEmbed and was slightly below MeanEmbed.
The passage notes no statistical tests but omits the single-evaluation design and all specified missing-standard-error limitations.
The passage reports weakened out-of-domain shortening with correct length values, but omits both out-of-domain relative accuracies, leaving the mixed finding incomplete.
The passage covers Llama3’s same-generator superiority but does not report that Llama3 Method M had the highest T1 mean on each dataset.
It reports significant 2x fine-tuning gains across all settings but omits the stable-or-rising fine-tuned accuracy and mixed NFT pattern.
It addresses transfer but understates the result: e5 beat every Model M variant on all four metrics, including the near-tied Recall@200.
It reports the absence of significance testing but omits sparse/incomplete judgments and the resulting unreliability of recall-based assessments.
It reports some mixed baseline comparisons but omits Model M-40M’s weakness, model-size dependence, Recall@200, and gte-modernbert-base’s failure.
It accurately characterizes content results as mixed and reports representative correct metric directions; omitting some comparator-specific exceptions does not contradict the finding.
The edit variant is characterized against the beam variant, without stating the required edit-versus-vanilla comparison.
It reports the single-run design, absence of statistical tests, and resulting inability to claim significance; omitted evaluation details do not reverse this conclusion.
It addresses the negative transfer finding but restricts e5’s superiority to MRR and NDCG, omitting both recall metrics and the Recall@200 near-tie.
The four reported Method M p-values correspond to all named benchmarks and are each below 0.001, directly establishing the finding.
It reports lower full-method p-values throughout but omits the contrasting significance patterns of the two ablations, leaving the mixed finding materially incomplete.
The complete benchmark-specific p-values for Method M and all three baseline variants unambiguously encode the stated p<0.05 detection pattern.
It mentions small significant medical-role effects, but not that every alternative-embedding cell is significant or the effect-size separation with the robot exception.
It reports Method M+ cardinality relative to CERT-ED but omits Method M’s mixed results, leaving the finding’s method scope incomplete.
It gives Method M’s disadvantage only on Yelp and LUN, omitting SpamAssassin and Method M+’s lower accuracy versus CERT-ED across all datasets.
It incorrectly describes Method M as having higher WikiText scores, although its advantage is lower bits per byte, and omits three accuracy benchmarks.
It reports only general improvement on most metrics and two examples, without identifying the five improvements or two tiny decreases.
It claims Method M was higher on MMLU, ARC-C, and GSM8K, but the 1B results contain ties and a slight MMLU deficit.
Only the absence of statistical tests is reported; the single evaluation and unavailable standard errors are omitted.
It correctly compares Method M with CERT-ED across all datasets but omits the required RanMASK comparison, so the finding’s comparator scope is incomplete.
“Did not consistently outperform” understates the uniform result: both Method M and M+ had lower clean accuracy than CERT-ED on every dataset.
“Matched or slightly exceeded” understates the four substantial advantages and omits that FOCUS outperformed Method M on GSM8K.
The passage gives general similarity plus MMLU and WikiText examples, but omits the ARC-C, GSM8K, and Belebele relationships.
It reports a gap on ARC-C despite exact preservation and omits Method M’s worse Belebele performance.
It notes absent statistical tests but does not report the single evaluation or the metrics lacking standard errors.
The passage addresses inconsistency but wrongly calls HotpotQA/BGE generator performance a loss; Method M tied the best baseline at 60.9.
“Did not consistently outperform” understates the uniform result that neither Method M nor M+ improved clean accuracy over CERT-ED on any dataset.
The displayed gains are correct, but calling these the three evaluated losses wrongly excludes four additional paired losses with positive average gains.
It reports the lack of significance tests, but incorrectly limits testing to three KD losses and omits key evidence limitations.
The three displayed gains are accurate, but “three evaluated KD losses” understates the reported scope by excluding four omitted paired losses.
It correctly notes absent significance tests, but “three KD losses tested” is false given four additional reported paired losses and understates the evidence scope.
It addresses failed transfer but omits Recall@200, where Model M-110M trailed e5 by only 0.001, overstating the unqualified non-generalization conclusion.
It portrays transfer only as uniform underperformance to e5, omitting the baseline-specific mixed recall pattern, size dependence, and gte-modernbert-base’s failure.
The passage separately compares fine-tuned Method M with ZeroGen and NFT, but does not report the NFT-versus-ZeroGen pattern or its generator-specific interpretation.
It reports significant 2x superiority over NFT, but not that fine-tuned accuracy stayed stable or rose while NFT results were mixed.
It omits BN and conflates variants on MR: M-static decreased MR BLEU, whereas only M-dynamic improved it slightly.
It explicitly reports that no significance tests were conducted, correctly conveying that statistical reliability was not established.
The passage correctly covers MMLU, ARC-C, GSM8K, and WikiText relative to the original model but omits the Belebele decline.
The passage correctly establishes that several filters beat Method M on individual MMLU combinations; the reversed Rand comparison is incidental and does not alter F5.
It implies success across all RankT5 datasets, but incorrectly identifies HotpotQA’s 0.3-point gain as largest; Musique’s gain was 0.4.
It reports the 2WikiHop/BGE loss, but the aggregate “matched or exceeded” wording does not report Musique’s win and HotpotQA’s tie separately.
It accurately covers medical personas only; it omits universal significance across personas and the medical/non-medical effect-size contrast, including the robot exception.
Although the three displayed gains are correct, describing them as all evaluated KD losses omits four additional paired losses reported in the note.
It accurately conveys that available evidence is limited to GPT-2 results and lacks standard deviations and statistical tests; omitted details do not contradict that limitation.
The passage omits Method M’s Llama3-8B round-4 deficit, so it does not report the finding’s full cross-model, cross-round pattern.
The listed Method M p-values cover all four intentionally included benchmarks and are all below 0.001.
It covers the full method’s lower p-values but not that no-watermark remained significant throughout while no-pairing was significant only for GSM8K.
Its complete p-value lists for every method and benchmark establish exactly which baseline variants crossed p<0.05 and that Method M always did.
“Mixed” summarizes only M-dynamic and omits both the language-specific pattern and M-static results required by the finding.
The passage reports M-dynamic’s DE and ZH improvements but omits the finding’s contrasting M-static results.
The comparison reports increases for only BLEU, COMET-KIWI, and XCOMET, omitting the required COMET increase.
The passage covers Llama3’s same-generator superiority but does not state that Llama3 Method M attained the highest T1 mean on both datasets.
Although the baseline caveat is correct, claiming no statistical test for 2x contradicts the paired-test significance markers defined for those rows.
The passage addresses cross-dataset transfer and correctly reports weaker length reductions, but omits the corresponding out-of-domain relative accuracies required by F5.
The passage gives only a majority-level baseline comparison; it does not establish Method M’s lower p-value for every baseline variant on every benchmark.
Both unseen-data settings are covered and the conclusion is correct; the misstated held-out minimum remains above 0.05 and does not change the finding.
It reports only that baselines mostly exceeded 0.05, collapsing distinct LLM DI variants and omitting each baseline’s benchmark-specific detection pattern.
The passage compares the edit variant with the beam variant, not with vanilla LLaMa-3-8B as required.
It correctly reports worse or unchanged structural adherence and reduced ROUGE-L versus vanilla; omission of the FactCC increase leaves the stated claims accurate.
It correctly presents the trade-off of lower ROUGE-L but higher FactCC and AlignScore for the stated comparators, without falsely generalizing to Claude.
The edit variant is described and implicitly contrasted with beam, but the required comparison with vanilla LLaMa-3-8B is not reported.
The listed values concern separate fine-tuned-versus-ZeroGen and fine-tuned-versus-NFT comparisons; the passage does not report NFT’s mixed comparison with ZeroGen.
It correctly reports significant 2x superiority in all four settings but omits the finding that fine-tuned accuracy was stable or higher while NFT was mixed.
The passage correctly covers M-dynamic on DE and ZH but does not report the finding’s mixed M-static results.
It reports lower values without FILTER/NN for three metrics but omits COMET, so the all-four-metric finding is not fully reported.
The majority and exception statements do not establish lower Method M p-values for every PaCoST and LLM DI comparison across all four benchmarks.
It identifies LLM DI-different’s two detections but understates LLM DI-same’s complete failure and omits PaCoST’s sole TriviaQA detection.
NFT is not directly compared with ZeroGen, and the passage does not state that Llama3 gains largely depend on fine-tuning while Zephyr gains are partly retained.
The all-setting 2x superiority and significance are reported, but the stable-or-rising fine-tuned trajectory and mixed NFT trajectory are not.
The broad better-preservation claim and selected examples do not report superiority across all six accuracy benchmarks and lower WikiText in the 12B setting.
It summarizes improvement on most metrics but omits the complete five-improvement and two-decrease pattern.
General near-equivalence within 0.01 does not report the exact ties, slight MMLU deficit to MeanEmbed, or Belebele and WikiText advantages.
The passage reports no statistical tests but omits the single-evaluation design and the specified missing standard errors.
